butchering-prepare-desc: Keep a knife ready and build your processing area before bringing meat home. The flint skinning hook and primitive butchering table provide a stone-age route; iron and a cleaver are not prerequisites. Read their current handbook recipes and reserve space for the table. Tick when you have chosen a suitable site and prepared a knife.
butchering-hook-desc: Knap flint hooks, then use the handbook recipe for a flint skinning hook. Place the station with room beneath it. The hook uses a knife for skinning: a cleaver is not a substitute here. Tick when the hook is ready.
butchering-table-desc: Build a primitive butchering table using its handbook recipe. It occupies a backpack slot for transport; place it like a filled skep using Ctrl with the backpack-slot controls. Leave room for its three-block footprint, extending two blocks to the right. The recipe consumes a stone knife and axe: keep or make another working knife for the hook before hunting. Tick once placed and accessible with a working knife.
butchering-retrieve-desc: Hunt a supported animal, then right-click its unharvested corpse with an empty active hand. Large corpses need an open backpack slot; small chickens, hares and foxes can fit ordinary inventory slots. Corpses slow you and spoil, so return promptly. Cutting it in the field remains an emergency option with reduced yield, not the station route. This is animal processing, not player grave recovery. Tick after bringing one corpse to your hook.
butchering-skin-desc: Right-click the corpse onto the hook, then hold right-click with a knife until skinning finishes. Collect the skinning products appropriate to that species: hides, fur or feathers are not interchangeable. The corpse must remain on the hook for bleeding. Tick after skinning one corpse.
butchering-bleed-desc: Leave the skinned corpse on the hook. It cannot be removed during bleeding. Allow game time to pass: small, medium and large workloads require more than one, two or four game hours respectively. When it becomes bled out and less red, take it down empty-handed. No separate dressing station is needed. Tick after retrieving the bled-out corpse.
butchering-process-desc: Place the bled-out corpse on the butchering table. Hold right-click with a knife or cleaver until processing finishes; a cleaver uses less durability here. Collect the available meat and other products promptly. Species and condition affect yield, so no particular rare product is required. Tick after processing your first corpse.
butchering-blood-desc: Before bleeding finishes, place an empty bucket directly beneath the hook, two to four blocks below. Retrieve the collected blood; catching it is optional and does not advance the corpse by itself. Use blood only in recipes that accept it: inspect available cookery before committing the batch. Tick after collecting blood in a bucket.
butchering-preserve-desc: Choose a preservation route that accepts your actual meat. Butchering also offers smoking on a rack with a firepit below; inspect the rack and food handbook before starting. Store or cook the result before it spoils. Expanded Foods and its cookery modules offer additional uses when installed, but none is required here. Tick after preserving or cooking a product from your first table batch.
butchering-offal-desc: If your animal yielded bloody offal, use the handbook barrel-cleaning recipe before its food recipes. Do not expect every species to supply it. This is an optional use for an actual product, not a requirement to hunt a rare animal. Tick after cleaning a batch of offal.
butchering-sinew-desc: If you obtained wet sinew, dry it before using the dried product in a compatible bow, sewing or glue recipe. Use its handbook entry for the current drying and ingredient rules. Tick after drying sinew and selecting a use for it; this branch is optional.
butchering-bones-desc: Some animals leave a bone carcass after table processing: break it for bones. Inspect bone and strong-bone recipes for a useful tool or material. Not every species provides the same remains. The pack disables the bone pickaxe, and some special recipes are class-gated; choose an available recipe instead. Tick after recovering and using an available bone product.
butchering-bag-desc: Butchering bags can help transport corpses; inspect the chosen bag recipe and capacity rather than assuming every corpse fits. Decide whether a bag or a better processing tool will improve your next trip. A cleaver improves table work but still cannot skin on the hook. Tick after preparing an appropriate transport or tool upgrade.
butchering-hunt-desc: Chickens are easy prey; larger animals fight back. Butchering lets you bring an unharvested corpse home with an empty active hand. Prepare the hook and table before the next hunt: follow the Butchering chapter from Prepare before hunting. Field cutting remains available at reduced yield. This quest still records a chicken kill, not completion of carcass processing.
butchering-leather-desc: Take a raw hide from the hook into the Leatherwork chapter. Skinning does not make finished leather: follow get-hide, soak-hide, scrape-hide, prepare-hide and make-leather, alongside weak and strong tannin. With Immersive Woodworking configured for tanning bark, use bark-based tannin recipes rather than vanilla logs. Tailor's Delight adds optional hide bundles and changes finished goods: inspect the installed recipes. Oiling a hide is a separate pelt route, not proof of tanned leather. Tick after choosing and starting the appropriate hide-processing route.
